subject: Prod access pattern anomaly — notification and evidence onboarding for Phoenix Health
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@phoenix-health.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com
Cc: security@phoenix-health.com
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Potential data exposure on prod-1 — immediate notice

Marissa —

We detected unusual traffic coming from a service account linked to our Phoenix Health integration (prod-1) between 02:30–02:45 UTC this morning. The requests appear to have pulled a small subset of user-level metadata (user ids, non-sensitive tags) from an S3-backed cache you host. At this time we do not have evidence of PII access but we are escalating out of caution.

What we need right away:
- A confirmation you received this notice
- A copy of your Incident Response Plan (IRP) or a pointer to the canonical document for customer use
- Any available telemetry slice covering 02:00–03:00 UTC (access logs, auth logs, token usage)
- A contact and time window for a call (we can do 30 minutes from now)

We also require a SOC 2 / SIG mapping for how this event intersects with your logging and retention controls — our security team will be running a quick review.

I can be reached through this address or at +1 (415) 555-0123.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Security Ops
Phoenix Health

Subject: Internal: Phoenix Health — evidence collection & SOX/SIG ask (do not forward)

Team —

Summary: Phoenix Health reports anomalous requests from a service account tied to their prod integration. External says user ids and metadata may have been accessed. No confirmed PII yet. I’ve acknowledged and committed to an initial bundle within an hour. Please treat as incident-level NVL-2.

Immediate asks (owners):
- Karthik: pull KV cache read logs, authentication issuance logs, and the model-serving access trace for host prod-1 covering 2029-09-12T02:00:00Z to 2029-09-12T03:00:00Z. Include token IDs and caller IPs where available. Label and checksum the exports.
- Jonas: snapshot the inference host (ephemeral metadata only), preserve container runtime events, and capture any k8s audit logs for the same window. Put encrypted bundle onto secure share: /shared/phoenix-health/forensics-20290912.
- Laura: prepare a SOC 2 control crosswalk and SIG matrix for logging, retention, and access controls (control IDs and evidence pointers). We need to be explicit about what we log by default vs what Phoenix requested.

Notes on customer communications:
- Do not share raw PII. If an export contains PII, redact and explain redaction method.
- Keep chain-of-custody metadata inside the manifest.

Attachments to produce: forensic_manifest.pdf, log_excerpt.jsonl, custody_chain.txt. Mark all files with HSM-signed checksums.

I’ll coordinate the 09:00 PDT call and handle customer updates.

Marissa

- forensic_manifest_20290912.pdf — manifest with chain-of-custody and file checksums (attached)
